summary: Where we are: the vendor demo as shipped did 0.72 M TPM per GPU. A Triton recompile patch, 8 tokenizer workers, DSpark on CUDA graphs, production's 4×tp2 worker shape, a lifted verify-graph envelope (32 per rank) and a gateway that uses all 8 DP ranks now give 3.97 M per GPU on the static frame (57% of the 7 M north star, TTFT 3.3 s). A kernel fix (P1) restores fast cold prefill, and chain15 re-runs the frontier setup with both, plus a DSpark draft fix. Production itself is at 2.79 M per GPU of observed load (3.9 req/s per node, TTFT p50 0.34 s) and is not saturated.

The affinity gateway pins each session's prefix to one engine and one DP rank, so caches stay warm (88.5%) and the 4×tp2 layout's faster decode (2-rank lockstep instead of 8) shows: it holds p50 ≤ 2 s up to the 4× level, where the tp8 engine had already backed up by minutes. tests.note: Yes, they differ a lot: the same node shows 3.2–3.7 M/GPU on the static frame and 1–1.5 M/GPU sustained on real traffic. The gap is not error: static requests are 100% cached and identical, while real requests carry 5–60k uncached tokens each (9–12% of 50–650k prompts), and that prefill is most of the GPU time. The static frame also hides spec decode and routing effects, and the replay can rank layouts in the opposite order (tp8 vs 4×tp2 are equal on static, but only 4×tp2 + affinity holds 4× load on real traffic). The closed-loop replay isolates the prompt-mix effect (same load control as static, real prompts), so the three together separate 'prompt mix' from 'arrival pattern'.
